name: Copenhagen Plank
research: On the RIGHT side: root rot (0,-86,-90) = Ry(-86) lays him on his right side, Rz(-90) turns the body along Y: head +Y, chest faces -X (camera yaw -90 sees the chest and the body line), left side up, head end 4 deg higher. Right (support) shoulder must sit at forearm-on-floor height: upper arm 0.269 + elbow 0.045 = 0.315; rotated shoulder R offset z -0.187 -> root z 0.502. Then shoulders R (-0.076,0.483,0.315) / L (-0.076,0.453,0.754), hips L (-0.051,-0.005,0.612) / R (-0.051,0.011,0.392). Support arm: world down in the torso frame = (-0.998,0,-0.07) -> R elev 86, plane 0 (upper arm vertical), elbow 90 with bend [0,1,0] = forearm on the floor pointing toward the chest side (-X), fist thumb-up (axis torso +X = world up). Top arm rests along the flank (elev 15, elbow 20). Long lever (Marusic 2026 S2): top leg straight, hip-ankle 0.905, ankle on the flat bench pad (top 0.44 + 0.045 ankle half-width) -> dz = 0.485-0.612, dy = -sqrt(0.905^2-0.127^2) = -0.896 -> ankle L (-0.051,-0.901,0.485). Bottom leg straight under the bench: ankle R z 0.285 (pad underside 0.365) -> dy -0.899 -> (-0.051,-0.888,0.285). Bench flat (deg 0), rot_z 180 puts the seat end toward the athlete: seat edge at world y = -1.18 + 0.36 = -0.82, so the top ankle sits 0.08 m in on the pad; seat post at y -1.00 and front foot bar at y -0.70 (z 0.05) stay clear of the bottom leg (~z 0.3). Feet rot = body rot (toes toward the chest side, neutral ankle); explicit R feet/knees because rot does not mirror. Knee poles toward the chest side (-X). Sources S1 Serner 2014, S2 Marusic 2026, S3 Hinnekens 2024, S4 Garage Strength.
